Risk_Title: PHI entered into internal AI assistant
Risk_Description: Employees paste PHI or customer confidential data into Bluefin Assist prompts, creating unauthorized uses or disclosures and exposure if logs are retained.
Existing_Controls: Enterprise LLM access through the cloud provider under the existing BAA; SSO; provider does not train on prompts.
Planned_Treatment: Adopt the AI Acceptable Use Policy; deploy DLP scanning on prompts for PHI patterns; add a PHI warning banner; cover AI data handling in training.
Other_References: OWASP LLM02 Sensitive Information Disclosure; HIPAA Privacy Rule

Risk_Description: An internal survey found 31% of employees use personal AI accounts for work. Customer data or PHI entered into consumer tools without a BAA could be a reportable HIPAA breach.
Planned_Treatment: Publish an approved AI tools list; block unapproved AI services at the secure web gateway; give all staff access to Bluefin Assist as the sanctioned alternative; run quarterly shadow AI discovery.

Risk_Description: Direct or indirect prompt injection (for example, instructions hidden in ticket text) makes the chatbot reveal its system prompt or another tenant's ticket data, or misuse its ticket tools.
Existing_Controls: Retrieval is limited to public help-center articles; chatbot requires customer login.
Planned_Treatment: Enforce tenant-scoped retrieval and least-privilege tool permissions; add input and output filtering; require confirmation before ticket changes; red-team each major release.
Other_References: OWASP LLM01 Prompt Injection, LLM06 Excessive Agency, LLM07 System Prompt Leakage

Risk_Description: Support Copilot gives confident but wrong configuration guidance or misstates Bluefin's security commitments, causing customer misconfiguration or contractual disputes.
Existing_Controls: Answers are grounded in help-center articles.
Planned_Treatment: Show source citations; hand off to a human agent below a confidence threshold; block answers on contractual and security commitment topics; evaluate against a 200-question test set before release.

Risk_Title: No AI disclosure to chatbot users
Risk_Description: Users are not told they are chatting with AI. Article 50(1) transparency obligations have applied since 2 August 2026 and will cover EU users from the 2027 Netherlands pilot.
Planned_Treatment: Add a persistent AI disclosure label and first-message notice; document the disclosure in the system record.

Risk_Title: Chatbot cost abuse or denial of service
Risk_Description: Automated abuse of the chatbot drives excessive model API costs or degrades availability.
Planned_Treatment: Add per-user rate limits, token caps, and spend alerts.

Risk_Description: ReadmitIQ uses prior utilization and payer type, which can act as proxies for race and income. The model may under-predict risk for underserved groups, who then receive less follow-up care.
Planned_Treatment: Test performance by race and ethnicity, sex, age, and payer; justify or remove proxy variables; monitor subgroup performance quarterly; give customers the information they need for their own Section 1557 due diligence.
Other_References: HHS Section 1557 (45 CFR 92.210) for covered-entity customers

Risk_Description: Changing patient populations and new customer sites degrade ReadmitIQ accuracy without anyone noticing, so care managers act on wrong scores.
Planned_Treatment: Monitor AUROC, calibration, and drift per customer with alert thresholds; validate locally before each new site goes live (including EU sites); define retraining triggers.

Risk_Title: Unclear rights to use training data
Risk_Description: ReadmitIQ was trained on PHI from 12 customers. If the BAAs do not permit this use, or de-identification was not done to HIPAA standards, Bluefin faces HIPAA violations and contract breaches.
Existing_Controls: Data was reportedly de-identified using the Safe Harbor method, but this is undocumented.
Planned_Treatment: Legal review of all 12 BAAs; obtain an Expert Determination or document Safe Harbor de-identification; update contract language for de-identified data use; keep data lineage records.

Risk_Description: Care managers treat the score as a decision rather than one input and skip outreach to patients scored low risk.
Planned_Treatment: Show top contributing factors with each score; publish intended-use and human-oversight guidance; provide customer training materials.

Risk_Description: Bluefin has not determined whether ReadmitIQ is medical device software under EU MDR or FDA rules. If it is, the EU pilot would require CE marking, and EU AI Act high-risk obligations would apply from 2 August 2028.
Planned_Treatment: Obtain a written regulatory determination; document intended purpose; limit EU pilot scope until resolved; plan conformity assessment if needed.
Other_References: EU MDR 2017/745; FDA clinical decision support software guidance

Risk_Description: Hospitals cannot complete their own AI due diligence without information on model inputs, performance, and limitations, which stalls sales and renewals.
Planned_Treatment: Publish a model facts sheet: inputs (flagging protected-characteristic variables), training data summary, subgroup performance, limitations, and update history.

Risk_Description: An attacker with API access uses repeated queries to infer whether a patient was in the training data or to extract the model.
Planned_Treatment: Rate-limit and log scoring requests; round output scores; alert on anomalous query patterns.

Risk_Description: A roadmap item would extend StaffSense to recommend shifts for individual nurses. That would make it an Annex III high-risk system for EU customers and could trigger US automated decision-making laws.
Planned_Treatment: Require AI use-case intake and classification before roadmap commitment; keep aggregate-only design unless the committee approves.

Risk_Description: SaaS vendors enable AI features (meeting note-takers, summarization) that record and process customer calls containing PHI, and some may train on that data.
Planned_Treatment: Add AI questions to vendor risk assessments; require no-training and retention clauses; review AI feature settings quarterly; restrict note-takers on customer calls.

Risk_Description: The sales call-intelligence platform infers emotion from employees' voices. Emotion recognition in the workplace is prohibited under the EU AI Act, and this would apply to Amsterdam staff from 2027.
Planned_Treatment: Disable voice-based emotion and sentiment features tenant-wide; get written confirmation from the vendor.

Risk_Description: The applicant tracking system's ranking feature may disadvantage protected groups. It is high-risk under Annex III(4)(a) for EU candidates, and state and city hiring laws apply in the US.
Planned_Treatment: Obtain the vendor's bias audit; require human review of every rejection; notify candidates of AI use; assess disabling auto-ranking for EU roles.
Other_References: Colorado SB 26-189; NYC Local Law 144; Title VII

Risk_Title: No AI governance or inventory process
Risk_Description: New AI features and tools are adopted without risk review, so new risks are invisible until something goes wrong.
Existing_Controls: Point-in-time inventory created by this assessment.
Planned_Treatment: Charter the AI Governance Committee; require the AI use-case intake form for all new AI; maintain the inventory in the GRC system.

Risk_Description: Staff lack training on AI risks and limitations. Article 4 requires measures to support AI literacy for staff who use or operate AI systems.
Planned_Treatment: Launch role-based AI literacy training (all staff, engineers and data scientists, support agents, recruiters); track completion.

Risk_Description: Harmful outputs, bias complaints, or jailbreaks have no defined response process, and future serious incident reporting duties cannot be met.
Planned_Treatment: Add AI incident playbooks and customer notification criteria to the IR plan; run an AI tabletop exercise.

Risk_Description: The model provider updates or retires the underlying model, unexpectedly changing Support Copilot behavior, or has an outage.
Planned_Treatment: Pin model versions; run the regression test set before upgrades; fall back to human support on outage.
